caseStudy: Case Study 1: Weaponizing active developer AI sessions to deploy the Shai-Hulud worm
handling: The Mandiant report does not publish concrete indicators (no hashes, IPs, or domains) for this case study. All host indicators below are logically consistent SYNTHESIZED canaries used only to generate realistic-looking artifacts for detection engineering. Nothing is installed, contacted, or exfiltrated; every network action is loopback with zero bytes.
reportedTtps: compromise SaaS provider to hijack an active AI coding-assistant session
AI assistant recommends attacker-poisoned external dependency
poisoned PyPI package installs an infostealer
harvest GitHub OAuth tokens from the active session
self-propagating Shai-Hulud worm across ~100 internal repositories
repository-secret theft and proprietary source-code exfiltration to attacker repo
poison a package in the organization's official namespace causing a downstream secondary infection
reportedDefensiveControls: enforce IDE/CLI verification hooks validating AI-recommended dependencies against cryptographic checksums and approved allowlists
isolate local credentials so extensions cannot access raw API keys, long-lived OAuth tokens, or secrets
restrict workstation network egress to route dependency traffic through secure internal repositories (e.g. Artifact Registry)
